rationale: The buyer is specific and credible: Salesforce DevOps engineers and ISV teams at companies with managed package CI/CD pipelines — these people operate inside company toolchains, have engineering budgets, and already spend on Salesforce tooling. The pain is genuine and recurring (every CI/CD run that gates on package release state). Buildability is feasible at a basic level (a wrapper around the Salesforce Tooling API, callable from a CI step, with a simple auth + API key model and Stripe), and delivery could be automated. However, this is a narrow niche within a niche (Salesforce ISVs doing 2GP), responsiveness is untested, and Salesforce's own roadmap could close the gap. Validate before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a hosted REST endpoint (or CLI) that accepts a Salesforce package version ID plus org credentials and returns whether it is released or beta — abstracting the slow Tooling API lookup so CI/CD pipelines get a fast, reliable gate check. The factory builds it as a Claude-assisted API wrapper deployed on a simple hosting service (Cloudflare Worker or similar), with a Stripe payment link for an API key subscription ($29–$49/mo per team), a short landing page explaining the CI/CD use case, and a self-serve signup form. Outreach goes to Salesforce developer communities (Salesforce Stack Exchange, Trailblazer Community, LinkedIn Salesforce DevOps groups) via targeted messages — only after the operator approves the batch. Delivery is fully automated: the API runs 24/7, billing is via Stripe, and Claude handles support emails; the operator's only recurring task is approving outreach sends and reviewing the monthly billing summary. The risk is market size: only a few hundred teams worldwide have this exact pain acutely enough to pay; validate with 20 cold outreach messages first.
notes: All build_gates pass at validate stage. Advance to build only after at least one confirmed reply expressing intent to pay. Narrow niche — validate market size explicitly.
